_about: The closing section of the suite results document, the interpretation layer the owner's review asked for. `intro`: the paragraphs of C.1 before the observations. `observations`: a list of {id, template}; each template is one sentence the generator fills from the run with the placeholders listed under `placeholders` (sections.closing_values); an observation whose values the run lacks prints as 'not computed'. `caveats`: the paragraphs after the observations (the shared host load; cold / warm as the recorded heuristic). `plots`: the captions keyed paired_latency and phases (C.2). `sections`: per table section (C3 MCP overhead decomposition, C4 front cost, C5 cold versus warm, C6 load telemetry, C7 per-chapter timing) a method paragraph, an observation paragraph with the run's figures and sample sizes as placeholders, and a limits paragraph, printed above the tables. The tables keep compare.json's figures. No stacked bar of phase medians: their sum is not the median of the wall. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*. Placeholders of overview.json (database, k, ...) work here too.

placeholders.mcp_over_local_p50 / _p90 / _max / _n: compare.json summary.mcp_overhead.minus_local_ms (warm MCP wall minus direct-local's first warm wall), signed
placeholders.backend_over_local_p50 / _p90 / _n: summary.mcp_overhead.backend_minus_local_ms (the service-timed host call minus direct-local), signed
placeholders.phase_submit_p50 / _p90 / _max / _n: summary.mcp_phases.submit_ms; likewise phase_queue_*, phase_backend_*, phase_terminal_lag_*, phase_paging_*, phase_backend_pattern_*
placeholders.front_net_p50 / _p90 / _n: the per-scenario front_overhead.net_ms of compare.json (direct-remote minus direct-local, net of the server time), pooled over every scenario
placeholders.warm_wall_dl_p50 / _p90 / _n: the first host-warm wall per scenario on direct-local (warm after an interrupted execution excluded); likewise warm_wall_dr_*, warm_wall_mcp_*
placeholders.paired_dl_mcp_n / _ratio_p50 / _ratio_p1: the scenarios with a host-warm wall on both direct-local and mcp: their count, the ratio mcp / direct-local (p50, p10, p90), the difference (signed) and how many differ by less than 1 s
placeholders.paired_dl_dr_n / _delta_p50 / _delta_p90: the scenarios with a host-warm wall on both direct arms: their count and the difference direct-remote minus direct-local
placeholders.load_samples / load_sra_mean / load_sra_: the sampler's figures (report.load_figures) and whether the Logan caveat applies ('applies' / 'does not apply')
placeholders.warm_after_interrupted_n: executions that ran warm after an interrupted one (counted in no bucket)
placeholders.mcp_phase_largest / mcp_phase_largest_p5: the phase of summary.mcp_phases (submit, queue, backend, terminal lag, paging) with the largest p50, in words, and that p50
placeholders.load_caveat_line: one sentence: the Logan caveat applies (the sra_all CPU mean and the load1 mean over the samples) or does not

title: Cross-cutting timing
intro: What this section measures: the timings of this run as recorded, keyed on the host-cache heuristic of I.2 and read across the chapters; the observations below are computed from the run with their sample sizes, and the sections after the plots give each table its method, its observation and its limits. What it does not measure: the host's cache (a recency heuristic, never residency), the service's floor (one deployment, one day, under the host's load) or an end-to-end total (the phases' medians are never summed).

observations.template: Via MCP a host-warm request took {mcp_over_local_p50} longer than on direct-local at the median and {mcp_over_local_p90} at p90 (n {mcp_over_local_n} pairs; {mcp_over_local_no_queue_p50} and {mcp_over_local_no_queue_p90} with the queue wait taken out).

The host call as the service timed it differs from direct-local's wall by {backend_over_local_p50} at the median (p90 {backend_over_local_p90}, n {backend_over_local_n}): the overhead is the service's own phases, not the host.

Of the phases, {mcp_phase_largest} has the largest median ({mcp_phase_largest_p50}, n {phase_backend_n}); at the median submit takes {phase_submit_p50}, the queue {phase_queue_p50}, the backend {phase_backend_p50} and paging {phase_paging_p50}; the phases are shown side by side and never summed, since their medians do not add up to the wall's.

Per scenario the warm MCP wall is {paired_dl_mcp_ratio_p50} times direct-local's at the median (p10 {paired_dl_mcp_ratio_p10}, p90 {paired_dl_mcp_ratio_p90}; n {paired_dl_mcp_n}), a ratio driven by direct-local's milliseconds; {paired_dl_mcp_under_1s} of the {paired_dl_mcp_n} pairs differ by less than 1 s.

The public front costs {front_net_p50} per request at the median net of the server time (p90 {front_net_p90}, n {front_net_n}), plus a connection set-up of {connect_dr_p50} (p90 {connect_dr_p90}) against {connect_dl_p50} on the container's port.

Warm minus cold per scenario is {cold_warm_mcp_delta_p50} at the median via MCP (ratio {cold_warm_mcp_ratio_p50}, n {cold_warm_mcp_n}) and {cold_warm_dl_delta_p50} on direct-local (n {cold_warm_dl_n}): the host-cache heuristic separates little at this load.

The host's `sra_all` CPU averaged {load_sra_mean} % and load1 {load_load1_mean} over {load_samples} samples, so the Logan caveat {load_caveat}; {warm_after_interrupted_n} executions ran warm after an interrupted one and are in no bucket.

caveats: {load_caveat_line} Every timing in this section is the shared host's under that load: an upper bound for this day, not a baseline for the release.

Cold and warm are the recorded heuristic (a scenario's first execution to reach the host, then any within {warm_window_s} s of another ending on the host), not a measurement of residency; a delta between them is the difference of two executions in the loop's order, and the loop's order is the only control.

plots.paired_latency: Paired host-warm walls per scenario: the warm MCP call against direct-local (left, n {paired_dl_mcp_n}) and direct-remote against direct-local (right, n {paired_dl_dr_n}); log scales, the dashed line y = x. One point per scenario; nothing is summed.
plots.phases: The MCP phases of the host-warm calls whose backend was reached, one box per phase: the box p25 to p75, the line p50, the whiskers p10 and p90, log scale (n per phase in the labels). The phases are drawn side by side, not summed: their medians do not add up to an end-to-end total.

C3.title: MCP overhead decomposition
paragraphs: *Method.* Pairs of host-warm executions only: the MCP warm execution (repeat 1 preferred) minus each direct arm's first host-warm execution of the same scenario, {mcp_over_local_n} pairs against direct-local and {mcp_over_remote_n} against direct-remote. The phases are the service's own measurements per MCP execution (n {phase_backend_n}): submit (the tool's acknowledgement), queue (the job created to started), backend (the host call), terminal lag (the job finished to the client seeing it) and paging (fetching the results).

*Observation.* The MCP arm's wall time exceeds direct-local's by {mcp_over_local_p50} at the median and {mcp_over_local_p90} at the 90th percentile ({mcp_over_local_no_queue_p50} and {mcp_over_local_no_queue_p90} with the queue wait taken out), and direct-remote's by {mcp_over_remote_p50} at the median; the host call itself, as the service timed it, is {backend_over_local_p50} longer than the direct-local wall at the median and {backend_over_local_p90} at p90, the public URL and the front being in it. The phase with the largest median is {mcp_phase_largest} ({mcp_phase_largest_p50}). The phases' medians are medians of separate distributions: they are not summed, because their sum is not the median of the wall. A cold MCP call (the scenario's first on the host) took {mcp_cold_wall_p50} at the median and {mcp_cold_wall_p90} at p90 (n {mcp_cold_wall_n}).

*Limits.* The pairs leave out cold MCP executions, executions warm after an interrupted one and the {scenarios_without_warm_pair} scenarios without a warm pair. The service ran on its own host and the MetaGraph host carried the Logan load (C.6), so the overhead is this run's, not the service's floor; the host-bound part of it is read on the backend row, the service-bound part on the others.

C4.title: Front cost
paragraphs: *Method.* direct-remote minus direct-local on host-warm pairs of the same scenario, net of the server time (the host's own elapsed time cancels, so the difference is the network, the front and the client), per chapter; a fresh connection's set-up (TCP, and TLS on the public URL) is recorded apart as the connect time.

*Observation.* The front and the network add {front_net_p50} at the median and {front_net_p90} at p90 over {front_net_n} pairs; a fresh connection costs {connect_dr_p50} at the median and {connect_dr_p90} at p90 on the public URL (n {connect_dr_n}) against {connect_dl_p50} on localhost.

*Limits.* {warm_pairs_left_out_after_interrupted} pairs warm after an interrupted execution are left out. A chapter whose net cost sits above the run's median is one with bigger answers (larger bodies through the front), not a slower host; the laptop's own load is in the remote wall and is not sampled.

C5.title: Cold versus warm
paragraphs: *Method.* Per scenario the warm execution minus the cold one on the same arm (the delta, signed: negative when warm was faster) and warm over cold (the ratio). Only an arm with both states has pairs: mcp, cold then warm by construction ({cold_warm_mcp_n} pairs), and direct-local where a direct execution was the first on the host ({cold_warm_dl_n} pairs). Cold and warm are the recorded recency heuristic of I.2 (the scenario's first execution to reach the host; another within {warm_window_s} s), not a measured cache state.

*Observation.* On mcp the median delta is {cold_warm_mcp_delta_p50} and the p90 {cold_warm_mcp_delta_p90}, the median ratio {cold_warm_mcp_ratio_p50}; on direct-local the median delta is {cold_warm_dl_delta_p50}, the p90 {cold_warm_dl_delta_p90} and the median ratio {cold_warm_dl_ratio_p50} over {cold_warm_dl_n} pairs (a figure over fewer than about thirty pairs is anecdotal).

*Limits.* A negative median with a positive p90 says that most warm repeats were somewhat faster and some much slower; the slower ones are the service's queue and the host's load of that minute, not the cache. The heuristic cannot see what the host had cached before the run or whether another client warmed a row between the two calls, and the paired loop's order (direct after the cold MCP call) is the only control.

C6.title: Load telemetry
paragraphs: *Method.* docker stats of the staging container (CPU, memory) and of the `sra_all` container (the Logan indexing load) and the host load average, sampled every 2 s on mex and joined to each execution's window; per chapter and arm the table gives the container's peak CPU and memory, the `sra_all` CPU mean and the load1 mean over the executions.

*Observation.* {load_samples} samples; `sra_all` CPU mean {load_sra_mean} % (max {load_sra_max} %), load1 mean {load_load1_mean} (max {load_load1_max}), so the Logan caveat {load_caveat} (the thresholds: {load_caveat_sra_cpu_pct} % `sra_all` CPU or a load1 of {load_caveat_load1}, half of mex's cores).

*Limits.* The figures are the shared host's context, not the request's own cost: a container peak above 100 % says a chapter's requests ran threads in parallel, the memory peak is the loaded index's residency, and the `sra_all` and load1 columns say how busy the host was while each chapter ran. Nothing here attributes a slow execution to the load; it says only under which load it ran.

C7.title: Per-chapter timing
paragraphs: *Method.* Wall and server time per chapter, arm and host-cache state, as p50, p90 and max with n; {warm_after_interrupted_n} execution(s) warm after an interrupted execution are in neither bucket.

*Reading.* Compare arms within one chapter and one host state only. The server p50 of the three arms of one chapter should agree, since it is the same host's time on the same requests; a direct-remote server time above direct-local's is the loop's order (direct-remote runs third, warmer), not the front. A chapter whose host-cold p90 is far above its host-warm p90 is one whose requests read rows the host had not yet touched; its cold figures are the ones a first client sees.

*Limits.* The cold buckets of the direct arms are small by construction (a direct execution is cold only when the MCP call before it never reached the host), so their percentiles are those of a few scenarios; the mcp cold bucket is the whole arm. The Logan caveat of C.1 {load_caveat} to every figure here.
